tasks.short: Study technical sources and product samples to establish accurate operating procedures and production sequences.

steps.what: Collect current drawings, specifications, mockups and product references.
Read sources and map components, dependencies and operating conditions.

loop.input: Registered specifications and drawings for one product revision.
loop.output: Component and dependency map with page references and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate references and revision identifiers; writer verifies relationships and safety-relevant details.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per source section; unreadable or conflicting material becomes an open question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative specifications and drawing annotations describe relationships that fixed field extraction cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Inspect product samples and observe the actual operating sequence.
Discuss missing details and conflicting instructions with the technical engineer.
Document the operating procedure and production sequence from verified evidence.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence map, observation notes and engineer clarifications.
loop.output: Procedure and sequence brief with evidence references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections and source coverage; writer verifies order, conditions and warnings.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; unsupported instructions remain blank and are escalated.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning mixed technical evidence into clear procedural prose requires language synthesis.

steps.what: Approve technical accuracy and resolve remaining safety-critical uncertainties.

tasks.design: Configure revision-controlled source packs in the {DOCS}, with deterministic completeness checks and a bounded extraction loop producing an evidence map. A second bounded loop drafts the technical brief from reviewed evidence; physical observation, engineer clarification and technical approval remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources used different formats and revisions. Understanding physical behaviour and undocumented dependencies required direct inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document metadata and inexpensive custom extraction tools can assemble referenced evidence and draft structured briefs. Faster AI-assisted coding lowers implementation effort without resolving technical uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Complex drawings, undocumented operating conditions and safety-critical sequencing still require product knowledge and physical validation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice where observed behaviour contradicts the specification and ask the engineer the question that prevents a dangerous instruction.

ambition.what: Pre-release documentation readiness review identifying missing operating evidence.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time assembling sources and more time observing products and resolving gaps. They gain a proposed documentation-readiness recommendation; engineering retains technical approval.

reach.task: Review whether a procedure gives readers the prerequisites and sequence they need.
reach.learn: Task analysis, evidence traceability and procedural editing.

evidence.claim: Source-linked technical extraction and brief generation are proposed designs, not demonstrated technical-writing cases in this digest.
Acrolinx provides repeatable style checks and quality gates; this supports language checks, not engineering validation.
A controlled professional-writing trial found productivity gains; its results do not establish savings for equipment analysis.

assumptions: This describes a company that documents physical equipment or technical products.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Source assembly is repetitive, but physical inspection and engineering judgement limit overall automation.
Use access-controlled processing under GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations. Assess consultation under national rules where employee-facing changes warrant it.
unknowns: Whether drawings and specifications have reliable revision identifiers.
Whether product samples and technical engineers are available.
Which procedures require formal safety or regulatory approval.
Whether access, processor terms or national consultation requirements delay implementation.
research_questions: Can extraction preserve drawing relationships and references on representative source packs?
Which evidence gaps are most predictive of later documentation corrections?
new_work: Review extracted relationships and evidence references.
Maintain revision mappings and source permissions.
Handle unreadable drawings and unresolved contradictions.
Evaluate draft quality against approved technical briefs.

tasks.short: Arrange formatting, reproduction and controlled distribution of approved technical material.

steps.what: Send production requirements, source files and intended recipients to the publishing coordinator.
Prepare layouts and generate required digital and print versions.
Check the proof for missing content, broken references and layout errors.
Authorise the exact revision, audience, channels and print quantity.
Place the approved print order and confirm delivery requirements.
Release digital copies, notify recipients and record distribution.

tasks.design: Use structured production requests in the {WORKFLOW} and template-based generators fed by the {DOCS}. Bind release authorisation to the exact files, recipients and print order, then execute approved distribution through the {CMS}, {EMAIL} and {PROCUREMENT}; changed payloads require renewed approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layout preparation and distribution were coordinated through attachments and individual instructions. Publication metadata did not consistently travel with the files.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and publishing features handle much of the workflow. Small deterministic generators can fill remaining format and packaging gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Complex layouts, accessible output and physical printing exceptions need inspection. Incorrect audience selection remains consequential.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct publication is unsuitable for its audience, channel or release date.

ambition.what: Version-specific publication packs for service partners.

tasks.altitude: The writer reviews proofs and release exceptions instead of coordinating routine handoffs. Publication authority remains with the publication approver.

reach.task: Create reusable layouts for digital and printed technical material.
reach.learn: Template constraints, accessibility checks and print production requirements.

evidence.claim: Template rendering, approval routing and controlled distribution generally use deterministic software.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style checks and quality gates, a possible component of proof checking.

assumptions: Source material is normally digital; arranging typing now mainly means formatting and production.
Printed copies remain part of this representative workflow.
The review time for distribution gates is accounted for in the release-authorisation step.
Build ranges assume existing publishing and purchasing capabilities.
GDPR applies to recipient data; applicable EU AI Act duties apply if model-generated content enters the process. Consultation follows national rules where relevant.
unknowns: Which output formats, languages and accessibility requirements are mandatory.
Whether publication and purchasing systems expose usable approval mechanisms.
Whether print quantities require a separate budget approval.
Who may approve external distribution and recipient lists.
research_questions: Can existing configuration cover production requests and distribution without custom software?
Which layout defects require visual review rather than automated checks?
new_work: Maintain publication templates and rendering checks.
Resolve failed print orders and delivery exceptions.
Maintain recipient groups and distribution permissions.
Review proofs and approve changed release payloads.

tasks.short: Create and update online help that explains verified product behaviour and user procedures.

steps.what: Collect release changes, support issues and existing help articles.
Identify affected topics and decide which changes need new instructions.

loop.input: Release changes, de-identified support issues and indexed help topics.
loop.output: Proposed affected topics, coverage gaps and reasons linked to sources.
loop.check: Validate topic identifiers and citations; writer checks scope and priority.
loop.stop: One classification and one correction pass per release; unclear changes become open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text change descriptions and reader problems rarely share exact vocabulary with existing help topics.

steps.what: Draft or revise help topics, prerequisites and troubleshooting instructions.

loop.input: Approved topic plan, current articles and verified product evidence.
loop.output: Tracked article changes with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate schema, references and supported claims; writer reviews clarity and procedural completeness.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per topic; missing evidence blocks the affected instruction.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure but cannot compose clear instructions from varied source prose.

steps.what: Test instructions in a product test environment and resolve incorrect behaviour.
Check terminology, style, links, navigation and article formatting.
Approve article accuracy, reader suitability and release readiness.
Publish the approved revision and update the help index.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration assembles changes from the {PROJECT}, de-identified issues from the {HELPDESK} and current articles from the {CMS}. Bounded loops propose affected topics and source-linked drafts, while configured terminology and link checks handle routine quality control. The writer tests instructions, and the {CMS} publishes only the revision authorised by the documentation lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes and reader problems were scattered across teams. Drafting depended on interpreting incomplete descriptions and manually finding affected articles.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured article stores, change feeds and inexpensive integrations support repeatable intake. Bounded drafting can reduce prose work when verified sources are available.
tasks.still_hard: Documentation cannot establish product truth from incomplete release notes. Version differences, permissions and complex troubleshooting need hands-on validation.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate the user's mistaken assumption and test whether the instructions actually help them finish the task.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of help gaps using recurring support problems.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more of the week testing procedures and choosing which reader problems deserve attention. They gain delegated topic-priority decisions within the agreed release scope.

reach.task: Improve help navigation and contextual guidance at points of user confusion.
reach.learn: Information architecture, task-based usability testing and accessible interface copy.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable style-guide scoring and quality gates.
LanguageTool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation and style.
The professional-writing trial supports potential drafting gains but does not validate online-help accuracy or these time estimates.
The proposed change-to-topic mapping and publication integration are design estimates requiring customer validation.

assumptions: The company maintains versioned online help and a product test environment.
The prior suggesting near-total automation is tempered by source uncertainty, procedural testing and release accountability.
Publication-gate review time is counted in the approval step.

Support inputs are minimised and de-identified where possible under GDPR. Assess applicable EU AI Act obligations and consultation under national rules; technical help has no assumed journalistic exemption.
unknowns: Whether release changes reliably identify affected features and versions.
Whether support tickets can be processed under existing access and processor arrangements.
Whether help articles have stable identifiers and structured content.
Who has delegated topic-priority and publication authority.
Which procedures need additional engineering or compliance approval.
research_questions: How often does topic mapping miss an affected article in historical releases?
Can draft instructions pass task-based testing without substantial rewriting?
Which help gaps explain repeated support contacts?
new_work: Review proposed topic coverage and source-linked drafts.
Maintain article identifiers, templates and terminology.
Handle incomplete release information and failed checks.
Monitor integration failures and stale article mappings.
Test changed procedures and approve publication.

tasks.short: Review equipment source material to establish reliable operation, maintenance and service facts.

steps.what: Gather manufacturer catalogs, drawings and service documents for the equipment.
Check equipment identifiers, revision dates and source applicability.
Read operation, maintenance and service requirements and record supporting references.

loop.input: Applicable catalogs, drawings and service documents for identified equipment revisions.
loop.output: Referenced facts covering operating limits, maintenance intervals, service conditions and warnings.
loop.check: Validate units, identifiers and page references; writer checks conditions, exceptions and safety-relevant entries.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document section; unreadable details remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in prose, tables and annotations, with qualifications that fixed extraction rules can miss.

steps.what: Compare sources and identify missing, inconsistent or superseded requirements.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence entries and source-applicability exceptions.
loop.output: Potential contradictions and missing conditions with both supporting references.
loop.check: Compare numeric fields deterministically; writer verifies semantic conflicts and rejects false matches.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per equipment item; unresolved conflicts go to engineering.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different wording can conceal incompatible instructions even when identifiers and numeric values match.

steps.what: Resolve technical conflicts or record that further evidence is required.
Store reviewed facts, unresolved questions and source references for later writing.

tasks.design: Configure source intake from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} into the {DOCS}, then use deterministic equipment and revision matching to flag exceptions. Bounded extraction and reconciliation loops build referenced evidence and conflict registers. Engineering resolves technical conflicts, and the {DOCS} preserves approved facts alongside unresolved questions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier material was file-based, inconsistently indexed and difficult to compare. Similar equipment names concealed different revisions and service requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can populate a stable evidence schema, while simple identifier and unit checks catch routine mismatches. AI-assisted coding makes these small integrations cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Obsolete supplier files, conditional warnings and undocumented equipment modifications can invalidate apparently clear facts. Engineering may need supplier clarification or inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a catalog statement does not apply to the installed equipment and refuse to turn uncertainty into an instruction.

ambition.what: Equipment documentation gap register for maintenance planning.

tasks.altitude: The writer reviews evidence exceptions rather than repeatedly searching catalogs. They can recommend which documentation gaps need investigation; maintenance and engineering retain operating decisions.

reach.task: Check that technical claims carry the conditions and evidence needed for publication.
reach.learn: Source provenance, revision applicability and editing conditional instructions.

evidence.claim: Revision matching, unit validation and evidence registers can use deterministic software; mixed-document interpretation needs validation.
The digest provides no documented equipment-source extraction case establishing these proposed savings or build ranges.

assumptions: An equipment list and identifiable supplier documents are available.
Routine collection is automatable where authorised file access exists; inaccessible portals remain exceptions.
The reviewed evidence pack supports later writing and does not authorise operation or maintenance.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act obligations apply to processing. Supplier access and reuse rights require review; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges are estimates for a limited initial equipment set.
unknowns: Whether equipment identifiers distinguish installed modifications and revisions.
Whether supplier access permits automated retrieval and document processing.
Whether scanned drawings and catalogs are legible.
Who can resolve conflicts and obtain supplier clarification.
Which maintenance facts require formal engineering approval.
research_questions: How reliably can extraction preserve units, conditions and warnings in representative supplier documents?
Can deterministic revision matching separate current and obsolete instructions?
Which conflict types require physical inspection rather than document review?
new_work: Review extracted facts and proposed contradictions.
Maintain equipment identifiers and revision mappings.
Handle inaccessible or unreadable supplier sources.
Track unresolved engineering questions and superseded evidence.
Maintain access controls and extraction quality checks.

role.altitude: The technical writer spends more time testing procedures, investigating missing evidence and improving reader outcomes. They can gain topic-priority and documentation-readiness recommendations while engineering and publication approvers retain their decision rights.
reach: Editors: review evidence, conditions and procedural clarity.
Desktop publishers: develop accessible, reusable publication templates.
Web and digital interface designers: improve help navigation and contextual guidance.
skills_to_grow: Task analysis and procedural usability testing
Deterministic quality checks and integration requirements
Evaluating bounded extraction and drafting loops
Privacy-aware handling of support and technical sources
role.ambitious_version: Offer a documentation-readiness service that combines source-gap reviews, tested procedures and support-informed help priorities before each release.
